findings.title: Do not trust the ISR header in the shared render handler
findings.why_it_matters: A request to the ordinary render function can select a different Astro route by supplying both `x-vercel-isr: 1` and `x_astro_path`, defeating the existing path-override protection and potentially bypassing path-specific Vercel routing or access controls. The same entrypoint is built for both `_render` and `_isr`, so the header alone does not establish which function received the request. Restrict the override to a separately configured ISR entrypoint or another trusted signal that cannot be supplied by the caller.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the ISR function with a distinct entrypoint or build-time flag and accept `x_astro_path` only there; retain the existing secret-gated behavior in `_render`.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/test/path-override-security.test.js:30 -- it('ignores untrusted x_astro_path query param on _render', async () => {

residual_risks: The repository does not establish whether Vercel strips or replaces client-provided x-vercel-isr headers before invoking a function; deployment-level exploitability depends on that behavior.
